en: The Amoghapāśahṛdaya Dhāraṇī Sūtra,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of South India during the Tang Dynasty, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Bhagavat was dwelling on Mount Potalaka, in the palace of the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
That ground was filled with countless precious sāla trees and tamāla trees.
Circumambulated by various jewel-trees, such as the *campaka*, the *aśoka*,
and the *atimuktaka*.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of eight thousand bhikṣus,
ninety-nine koṭi-nayuta-hundred-thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devaputras from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens.
The Devaputra Īśvara, the Devaputra Maheśvara,
and the Devaputra Mahābrahmā were the leaders,
together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of other devas and humans.
Surrounded by those before and behind him, the Buddha preached the Dharma for them.
At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat and bared his right shoulder.
Placing his right knee upon the ground, he joined his palms toward the Buddha,
and with a serene countenance and a smile, addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, I possess a heart-mantra called Amoghapāśa."
In the ninety-first eon of the past,
there was a world named Vijaya;
its Buddha was named Lokendrarāja Tathāgata.
I received this *Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya-mantra* from that Buddha.
World-Honored One, because I have upheld this divine mantra,
I have converted immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devaputras of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens.
The Devaputra Īśvara and the Devaputra Maheśvara were caused to incline toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
by the power of these merits, they immediately attained ten billion samādhis.
Amoghaśrīprajñā is the foremost among them.
World-Honored One, wherever this dhāraṇī-heart mantra resides,
twelve billion devas, including Maheśvara and others, will come to that place to provide protection.
Just like a stūpa of the Buddha,
wherever this heart-mantra of the World-Honored One resides,
all sentient beings therein [shall be protected].
It should be known that such a person has already planted various roots of goodness under immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
World-Honored One, if there should be anyone who hears this dhāraṇī-heart mantra...
This person previously committed evil deeds and practiced what is contrary to the Dharma;
they insulted the virtuous and good, slandered the True Dharma,
and reviled all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas.
They will certainly fall into the Avīci Great Hell.
World-Honored One, if such a person, upon hearing this divine mantra-heart, gives rise to remorse and shame,
and observes the fast and precepts while reciting this divine mantra for one day and night.
One will then be able to extinguish all karmic offenses,
or else cause all one's karmic offenses to be experienced lightly in the present life.
If one contracts a feverish illness, [it shall be cured].
For one day, two days, or even up to seven days,
there may be pain in the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, lips, teeth, gums, palate, heart, abdomen, navel, flanks, hands, feet, limbs, joints, and so forth.
If one suffers from hemorrhoids, diarrhea, constipation, white leprosy, or great leprosy;
or from scabies, ringworm, black sores, red sores, discharging sores, or blisters;
or from diseases such as epilepsy, or from curses, incantations, and malevolent poisons.
Bondage, flogging, beatings, slander, and insults,
as well as other various evils that afflict the body and mind, along with all manner of ominous dreams—
I now declare these to be experienced in the present life.
Even the karma of the immediate transgressions is instantly extinguished;
how much more so for all sentient beings of pure faith who uphold this mantra—
how could their various sinful karmas not be extinguished?
Bhagavān, if there are sentient beings who,
with a mind of flattery, crookedness, and deceit,
hear this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya* mantra taught by me.
They falsely pretend to uphold [the teachings],
whether by writing them themselves, having others write them,
or explaining them to others so that they may hear and receive them.
Even if one recites this dhāraṇī-heart mantra into the ear of a being in the animal realm,
and contemplates the phrases of this divine spell because they are non-defamatory and signless.
Because it is unarisen, because it is non-conceptual,
because it arrives slowly, because it is effortless,
because it is free from defilement, because it is equanimous, because it does not abandon, and because it is free from the aggregates.
By practicing in this way through the application of skillful means,
and by the power of recollecting the Buddha’s qualities,
one thousand Buddhas will appear before one from each of the ten directions.
Upon seeing this, the practitioner’s entire stock of karmic offenses will be completely extinguished.
World-Honored One, I shall now speak briefly:
even those who merely transcribe this sutra [attain such merit].
If one places it within one's home and pays homage and makes offerings to it,
one will likewise obtain immeasurable and boundless merit;
how much more so for those who receive, uphold, read, and recite it!
Blessed One, if there are sentient beings who,
each for the sake of desiring to surpass others,
or out of fear of their masters, or out of fear of enemies and rivals, [act in such a way].
Out of fear of wild beasts, out of fear of perils and hardships,
or because they follow others, or because they seek nobility, or because they seek wealth and treasures,
they hear this Heart Sūtra of Divine Spells.
Even if they hear it and fail to give rise to reverence,
or even go so far as to slander, treat it with contempt, or disparage it,
by the power of the majestic spiritual authority of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, [it shall be protected].
This causes such a person to also generate supreme merit.
It is, for example, like someone who takes sandalwood, or aloeswood, musk, and so forth.
Even if one were to revile, disparage, crush, and grind these [fragrances] to smear them upon his body,
those perfumes and the like would never harbor such a thought as,
"This person is reviling me."
Just as sandalwood and other such substances perform the function of fragrance through their inherently fragrant nature, even if one were to begrudge its scent and not give it away,
O World-Honored One, this divine mantra-heart is likewise so.
Even if there are those who slander and revile it,
or those who, through flattery and deceit, copy, uphold, and make offerings to it,
they all create the causes and conditions for roots of goodness.
In every place of rebirth,
they never abandon the accumulations of ethical discipline, meditative concentration, wisdom, and merit; thus,
in future lives, they will be fully endowed with the fragrance of ethical discipline.
Bhagavān, if there be a son of good family or a daughter of good family,
or a bhikṣu, a bhikṣuṇī,
an upāsaka, or an upāsikā.
On the eighth day of the month, one should observe the fast with single-minded devotion,
refraining from all other speech, and recite this *Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya* mantra seven times.
That person shall, in their present body, obtain twenty kinds of sublime benefits.
What are the twenty?
First, the body is free from all remaining illnesses.
Second, any diseases resulting from previously committed karma are swiftly eliminated.
Third, his body will possess a radiant luster and skin so fine and soft that all who see him will rejoice.
Fourth, he will be loved and respected by the multitude, and he will closely guard his sense faculties.
Fifth, he shall obtain wealth and treasures.
Sixth, having acquired wealth and treasures, they shall not be plundered by thieves.
Seventh, they shall not be swept away by water or consumed by fire.
Eighth, they shall not be seized or robbed by the power of kings.
Ninth, all undertakings and activities will be successfully accomplished.
Tenth, the crops that are sown will not be damaged by adverse winds, torrential rains, frost, hail, or locusts.
Eleventh: If one recites this dhāraṇī-heart seven times and sprinkles the consecrated ashes and water in the eight directions, above, and below to demarcate the boundary,
all calamities and misfortunes shall be completely extinguished.
Twelfth, one shall not have one's vital energy (ojas) stolen by various malevolent spirits and the like.
Thirteenth, all sentient beings will love, delight in, and joyfully behold one.
Fourteenth, one shall not fear enemies or adversaries.
Fifteenth, should there be enemies or仇宿 (enmity), they will be quickly reconciled.
Sixteenth, one will not fear harm from humans or non-humans;
malevolent spells, sorcery, and evil spirits shall be unable to inflict injury.
Seventeenth, they will be free from intense afflictions (*kleśa*) and secondary afflictions (*upakleśa*).
Eighteenth, they will not die from injuries caused by fire, blades, or poisons.
Nineteenth, they will be constantly protected by the devas and benevolent deities.
Twentieth: wherever one is born, one shall not be separated from loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
These twenty kinds of sublime benefits should be sought after.
Furthermore, there are eight dharmas. What are these eight?
First, at the time of death, the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara manifests before that person in the form of a bhikṣu.
Second, at the time of death,
one will pass away peacefully and with ease, free from all suffering and pain.
Third, at the time of death, right mindfulness will manifest before them, and the mind will not become confused.
Fourth, at the time of death, their hands will not be disordered and their feet will not be drawn in or extended.
Fifth, at the time of death, they will not leak urine or excrement.
Sixth, even if one should fall ill, one will not be bedridden for long.
Seventh, at the time of death, one will not die with the face covered.
Eighth, at the time of death, one will attain inexhaustible eloquence.
Once their lives have ended, they will, in accordance with their vows,
be reborn in the pure lands of all Buddhas and never be separated from spiritual friends.
World-Honored One, if there are sons or daughters of good family who...
One shall abstain from wine, meat, pungent vegetables, and defiled or impure food.
Three times each day, at each session reciting three times,
one should chant this dhāraṇī-heart dharma-gate.
Supreme merit increases day and night.
Having understood that all sentient beings have varying capacities and strengths according to what they hear,
a bodhisattva should not harbor any secretiveness or stinginess in their mind.
Forever free from all evils of stinginess and jealousy,
and always acting for the benefit of all sentient beings,
may they swiftly proceed toward Bodhi and enter the stage of a Bodhisattva.
"Bodhi" is said to be prajñā;
"sattva" is precisely upāya.
These two kinds of dharmas...
They shall obtain all benefit and happiness for all sentient beings.
World-Honored One, I now wish to bring about the benefit and happiness of the fourfold assembly and other sentient beings who have committed transgressions.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will, out of compassion,
grant permission for me to recite this mantra-heart before the Tathāgata.
At that time, the World-Honored One...
He addressed the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"O sentient beings, now is the very time for purification.
I too rejoice in this divine mantra-heart."
In a future age, he will act as the father and mother for those who practice the Bodhisattva vehicle,
causing all the undertakings of these bodhisattvas to be swiftly accomplished.
At that time, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Gazing upon the Honored Countenance without averting his eyes for even a moment,
he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I pray that the Tathāgata will grant me leave to recite this divine mantra."
This dharma-gate of liberation, which all bodhisattvas should revere,
out of compassion for the world brings benefit,
welfare, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.
Those who wish to receive and uphold [this teaching] should first pay homage to the Buddhas of the three times,
as well as to the bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and śrāvakas;
they should pay homage to those who have attained the goal and those who practice correctly.
Furthermore, one should pay homage to the great-wisdom śrāvakas such as Śāriputra;
one should also pay homage to the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas headed by Maitreya;
and one should pay homage to the Tathāgata Suvarṇavarṇaprabhāsa-svara-vijitendra-rāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍita-rāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Amitābha.
Homage to the Tathāgata Supratiṣṭhita-maṇirājasaṃcaya.
Homage to the Tathāgata Samantaprabhāstutaguṇasañcayarāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vairocana. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnaśikhin.
Homage to the Tathāgata Lokavikhyāta.
Homage to the Tathāgata Skandhakṣatiprahīṇa.
Homage to the Tathāgata Kanakavarṇaśānta.
Homage to the Tathāgata Prabhāsa.
Homage to the Tathāgata Śāntamati.
Homage to the Tathāgata Suviśruta.
Homage to the Tathāgata Samantaprabhājitārindamaśrī.
Homage to the Tathāgata Indradhvajaguṇa.
Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnābhāsvara-svayambhū-rāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Anāvaraṇabhaiṣajyarāja.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vīranandin.
Homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Suvikrāntavikrama.
Homage to the Triple Gem.
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, who is endowed with great compassion.
Having thus paid homage to these noble beings, one should further reflect, saying: "Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara."
Having spoken this heart-mantra before the Tathāgata,
I shall now likewise speak this mantra.
May the undertakings I perform be swiftly accomplished.
"May all my fears be entirely dispelled.
At that time, the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this mantra:
